papers.title_en: From Slices to Volumes: Comparing 2D, 2.5D, and 3D Residual Networks for Pulmonary Nodule Malignancy-Risk Classification
papers.authors: Bahodir Nazarov, Zineb Gharib, Fatima Zazoul
papers.evidence: 比较2D、2.5D与3D残差网络用于医学图像分类。
papers.tldr: 肺结节CT恶性风险分类中，2D、2.5D与3D残差网络孰优缺乏受控比较。研究基于LIDC-IDRI构建患者不重叠队列，比较单层、五邻层与局部体积输入，并评估动量对比预训练、轻度增强及排除不确定标签。增强后2.5D测试Macro-F1最高（0.6537），高于2D（0.6134）和3D（0.5403）；增强普遍有效而预训练下降。结果支持2.5D折中方案，但维度归因受多因素限制。
papers.abstract_en: Purpose: To compare 2D, 2.5D, and 3D residual networks for pulmonary nodule malignancy-risk classification and evaluate momentum-contrast pretraining, mild augmentation, and exclusion of indeterminate ratings.   Methods: A retrospectively prepared LIDC-IDRI cohort contained 2,654 nodules labeled benign, indeterminate, or malignant using median radiologist ratings. Patient-disjoint splits comprised 1,876 training, 382 validation, and 396 test nodules. Representations included one axial slice, five neighboring slices, and a local CT volume. Each track evaluated a randomly initialized baseline, momentum-contrast pretraining followed by fine-tuning, and supervised training with mild augmentation. Checkpoints were selected by validation Macro-F1. The 2D experiments used three seeds; 2.5D and 3D results were single-run estimates. A separate binary experiment excluded indeterminate nodules.   Results: Augmented models achieved test Macro-F1 values of $0.6134\pm0.0075$ for 2D, $0.6537$ for 2.5D, and $0.5403$ for 3D; the 2D uncertainty denotes population standard deviation across seeds. Corresponding accuracies were $0.6128$, $0.6869$, and $0.5455$. Augmentation improved Macro-F1 within every track, whereas the tested pretraining recipes reduced it. Binary Macro-F1 values were $0.8227$, $0.8664$, and $0.7554$, respectively.   Conclusion: Augmented 2.5D achieved the highest observed performance. Differences in preprocessing, optimization, capacity, and replication limit attribution to dimensionality. Labels reflect radiologist-assessed malignancy risk rather than pathology-confirmed cancer. Code and experimental results are available at https://github.com/CT-DeepLearning-Team/CT-2D-2.5D-3D-DeepLearning.

papers.title_en: Active Reachability Learning for Humanoid Recoverability Monitoring
papers.authors: Zeyuan Feng, Baljeet Singh, Sarthak Ranjeet Kaingade, Somil Bansal, Bryan Trinh
papers.evidence: 面向人形机器人防跌倒的运行时监测
papers.tldr: 人形机器人任务策略部署需要运行时监测器及时预判不可恢复跌倒并触发回退。论文将监测器学习建模为回退策略的随机有限时域可恢复包络，并用价值学习与主动探索交替迭代：以reach-avoid问题引导不确定性探索，结合TD与蒙特卡洛目标提升分布内估值和不确定性估计，将高不确定区域视为不可恢复以抑制OOD乐观幻觉。在随机基准和29自由度Unitree G1上，监测覆盖率和准确性显著提升，并实现真实硬件零样本迁移。
papers.abstract_en: Deploying humanoid task policies requires reliable runtime monitors that anticipate unrecoverable falls in time to trigger a fallback. We formulate this task as learning the stochastic, finite-horizon recoverability envelope of a given fallback policy. Synthesizing this monitor is challenging: existing methods assume training data naturally covers the recoverability envelope, yet acquiring such data remains a major bottleneck for contact-rich systems. Consequently, they recover only a fraction of the true envelope, leaving them prone to optimistic hallucinations for out-of-distribution (OOD) inputs. We resolve this via a unified framework that iterates between value learning and active exploration. Data exploration is reframed as a reach-avoid problem, where an uncertainty-guided explorer systematically uncovers unseen states while avoiding confidently unrecoverable regions. This loop is further supported by a combined Temporal Difference and Monte Carlo objective for accurate in-distribution value prediction and reliable uncertainty estimation. By explicitly treating the remaining high-uncertainty regions as unrecoverable, the monitor mitigates optimistic OOD hallucinations. Evaluated on stochastic benchmarks and a 29-DoF Unitree G1 humanoid, our approach drastically improves monitor coverage and accuracy and successfully transfers zero-shot to real-world hardware.

papers.title_en: Sparsity-driven emergence of functional modularity in multitask neural networks
papers.authors: Bowen Shi, Qi Ouyang, Long Qian
papers.evidence: 稀疏正则化驱动网络结构模块化
papers.tldr: 多任务神经网络如何自发形成可复用模块尚不清楚。本文用稀疏正则训练多层感知机与轻量Transformer，并通过功能剖析识别任务选择性子网络（functional tokens）。这些模块在深层更易专门化，保留它们可维持对应任务而削弱其他任务；提取后还能重组重建复合计算而无需重训。结果表明稀疏约束不仅影响参数使用，也塑造学习计算的组织与复用。
papers.abstract_en: Neural networks can learn multiple tasks, but how learning organizes shared computation into specialized and reusable components remains poorly understood. In this work, we show that sparsity inducing regularization promotes functional modularity in multitask networks without predefined module boundaries. Using functional profiling in multilayer perceptrons and a lightweight transformer, we identified compact, task-selective subnetworks, termed functional tokens. Across rule-based task families, selectively retaining these tokens preserves their associated functions while reducing performance on other tasks. Such specialization develops preferentially in deeper layers during training, while earlier layers retain shared computation. Regularization strength and form shape module compactness and specialization, while task weighting alters functional allocation. Moreover, extracted functional tokens can be recombined through alternative pathways to reconstruct a learned composite computation without retraining, preserving their connectivity and learned weights. Our results suggest that sparsity-constrained optimization shapes not only parameter use but also the organization and reuse of learned computation.

papers.title_en: DT-JEPA: Learning to Predict Future Representations for Decision-Making
papers.authors: Changxu Ni, Yiyang Ni, Jun Li, Feiran You, Hongyang Du, Haitao Zhao, Shi Jin
papers.evidence: 结合世界模型式未来表征预测的离线强化学习
papers.tldr: Decision Transformer以预期回报作为动作条件，但回报难以完整描述未来状态转移，且依赖任务奖励标注。本文提出DT-JEPA，在潜空间设计概率预测器建模未来表示的条件分布，并采用无奖励离线预训练与在线微调框架。理论分析表明该目标最大化历史表示与未来轨迹互信息的变分下界，并给出有限样本性能界。D4RL实验显示其能高效适应多种离线强化学习任务，性能优于传统DT及其他离线RL方法，提升了无奖励数据利用与未见任务泛化能力。
papers.abstract_en: Decision Transformer (DT) has demonstrated strong performance in various offline reinforcement learning (RL) tasks by conditioning action generation on expected future returns and historical trajectories. However, treating expected future returns as the condition provides an incomplete description of the future, as trajectories with different state transitions and behaviors may share similar returns. Moreover, expected future returns inherently depend on task-specific reward functions, which makes policy learning reliant on reward-labeled datasets and restricts its scalability to tasks with similar but unseen rewards. Recently, Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA) have emerged as a promising paradigm of self-supervised learning-based world models, which learn predictive representations of future dynamics in latent space rather than reconstructing future states in the original space. Inspired by JEPA, we propose DT-JEPA, an offline pretraining and online fine-tuning framework that learns general knowledge from reward-free offline trajectories and achieves excellent adaptation to unseen tasks. Instead of predicting a single deterministic future embedding, we design a novel probabilistic predictor to model the conditional distribution of future representations in the latent space, thereby capturing both predictive information and uncertainty about future dynamics. Theoretically, we show that 1) the JEPA objective seeks to maximize a variational lower bound on the mutual information between historical representations and future trajectories; and 2) predictive future-conditioned policy learning admits a finite-sample performance bound with an O(N-1/4) estimation term. Experiments on D4RL benchmarks demonstrate that DT-JEPA achieves efficient adaptation across varying offline RL tasks, outperforming traditional DT-based and other offline RL methods.

papers.title_en: Certifying Distributionally Robust Decisions from Projection Observations
papers.evidence: 不确定性下基于投影观测的可认证稳健决策
papers.tldr: 在仅有标量高斯投影观测、潜在协方差与风险不可识别的设定下，研究分布鲁棒决策的可认证性。方法用观测律构造不可区分矩模型集合，并给出置信集证书：输出决策或未决；标量剖面把非线性风险比较化为凸内问题。理论上证明可靠性、不可区分且最优不相容时必要弃权，以及固定检查点认证保证。七个合成实例中联合校准矩区域给出的充分预算为显式样本信息下界的21至52倍，1900条模拟流零决策错误。
papers.abstract_en: A scalar measurement can determine a robust decision without identifying the latent covariance or every decision risk. We study finite Gaussian projection experiments with a fixed mean-plus-standard-deviation target. The observation laws define a set of indistinguishable moment models. We exhibit decisions that agree throughout that set despite unidentified risk values, and give a confidence-set certificate that returns a decision or an unresolved outcome. We prove soundness, necessary abstention for indistinguishable models with incompatible optima, and a fixed-checkpoint certification guarantee. A scalar profile reduces nonlinear risk comparisons to convex inner problems. Across seven synthetic instances, jointly calibrated moment regions give sufficient budgets 21 to 52 times explicit expected-sample information lower bounds. Separately measured stopping times are lower, with zero decision errors in 1,900 simulated streams. These comparisons do not constitute matching bounds, and the guarantees require Gaussian replication.

papers.title_en: Rollback: Experience Backtracking in World Models for Policy Improvement
papers.authors: Jiayi Luo, Yang Zhang, Liliang Chen, Nan Wang, Chen Gao, Boxiang Qiu, Zhuoxuan Li, Baorui Peng, Chuankang Li, Yuxiang Yan, Si Liu, Qingyun Sun, Shuicheng Yan, Maoqing Yao, Jianxin Li, Guanghui Ren
papers.evidence: 动作条件世界模型用于预测与策略改进
papers.tldr: 现有基于世界模型的机器人策略改进多把世界模型当作只能前向预测的替代环境，未利用可回退到过去决策点探索反事实的能力。Rollback将世界模型变为反事实引擎：回滚到关键决策点、分支替代动作并对比结果，将反事实结果蒸馏为动作级监督。在三个真实任务上，成功率较最强基线绝对提升10.67%、11.11%和11.85%，训练更稳定，并在8小时内于抛球和桌面冰壶上超过人类玩家平均成功率。该工作把世界模型搜索与异步真实机器人执行结合，形成自我强化循环。
papers.abstract_en: Action-conditioned world models offer a scalable alternative to costly real-world interaction for improving robot policies. However, existing world-model-based methods largely treat world models as forward-only surrogates of the physical environment, leaving untapped a capability no physical environment affords: rewinding to past decision points to explore counterfactual futures. We introduce Rollback, a policy improvement paradigm that turns world models from passive simulators into counterfactual engines: it rolls back to critical decision points, branches into alternative actions, and contrasts their outcomes to attribute success to individual decisions. This concentrates imagination where it matters most and distills counterfactual outcomes into fine-grained, action-level supervision without a separately learned value model. We build a scalable training system that unifies distributed world-model search with asynchronous real-robot execution, forming a self-reinforcing cycle: real-world experience continually sharpens the world model, and a sharper world model in turn drives further policy improvement. We term the world-model side of this cycle test-time physics grounding, a capability that hand-built physics simulators lack: while the world model serves as the training environment, real transitions from the policy it trains correct its dynamics through a lightweight LoRA pipeline. Experiments on three challenging real-world tasks show that Rollback improves success rates over the strongest baseline by an absolute 10.67%, 11.11%, and 11.85% on block extraction, ball tossing, and tabletop curling, respectively, while achieving more stable improvement throughout training. Although initialized from teleoperated demonstrations far below human level, Rollback surpasses the average success rate of human players on both ball tossing and tabletop curling within 8 hours of training.

papers.title_en: Action-Value Calibration via Continuation Sharing for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Yingjian Chen, Lang Zhou, Zixin Zhao, Pingfan Li, Weishi Zheng, Zhilin Zhao
papers.evidence: 强化学习策略优化中的动作价值与优势估计
papers.tldr: 长程智能体强化学习的信用分配依赖多步交互反馈，单条采样续写会让动作价值估计受后续决策干扰，局部信用不稳定。ConCal复用同一批次中共享状态动作转移的续写证据，将共享续写信息与各访问自身转移估计结合，递归校准价值并反向传播以细化早期动作价值。在ALFWorld和WebShop上，基于Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct，成功率较GiGPO分别提升3.39和5.86个百分点。该方法无需额外采样，降低对单条续写的依赖并缓解局部信用扭曲。
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning for long-horizon agents relies on feedback from sequences of interactions, making credit assignment to individual actions difficult. Existing methods such as GiGPO compare actions at shared states to compute relative advantages, but estimate each action's value from a single sampled continuation. The resulting local credit remains sensitive to decisions made later in the trajectory. To address this problem, we propose ConCal (Continuation Calibration), a recursive continuation-value estimator that incorporates continuation evidence already present in a rollout batch. ConCal matches visits from the same task by their incoming state-action-state transitions, combines shared continuation evidence with each visit's own transition estimate, and propagates calibrated values backward to refine earlier action-value estimates. This reduces dependence on individual sampled continuations and mitigates local credit distortions without additional rollouts. Held-out return diagnostics show lower error in within-group value differences and higher agreement with reference action orderings than estimates based on individual continuations. With Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, ConCal improves success rates over GiGPO by 3.39 and 5.86 percentage points on ALFWorld and WebShop, respectively. Our code is available at https://github.com/Yingjian-Chen/ConCal.

papers.title_en: Spiking Neuromorphic Control for Periodic Orbits Stabilization in Underactuated Robots: A Greedy Lyapunov-Based Approach
papers.evidence: 面向欠驱动机器人的Lyapunov非线性控制理论
papers.tldr: 针对欠驱动机器人周期轨道稳定化，论文研究事件驱动脉冲神经网络控制器。先对周期轨迹邻域做横向线性化，将轨道稳定转化为周期LTV系统零解镇定。再把原用于LTI的Lyapunov贪心设计扩展到周期LTV横向动力学，构造反馈控制器。蝴蝶机器人轨迹稳定验证了方法有效性，为脉冲神经形态控制提供可扩展的轨道镇定方案。
papers.abstract_en: This work investigates the use of event-based spiking controllers, implemented as spiking neural networks, for trajectory tracking in underactuated robots. Specifically, we address the problem of stabilizing a prescribed periodic orbit. It is well known that, by applying the method of transverse linearization to the robot dynamics in a neighborhood of a periodic trajectory, the dynamics can be approximately described by a linear time-varying system with periodic coefficients (a periodic LTV system). The problem of orbital stabilization can therefore be reduced to stabilizing the trivial solution of this LTV system. We show that a previously proposed Lyapunov-based greedy design, originally developed for LTI systems, can also be extended to the corresponding linearized transverse dynamics, which take the form of a periodic LTV system. This enables the construction of a feedback controller for orbital stabilization of the robot. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated on the trajectory stabilization problem for the butterfly robot.

papers.title_en: VLA-Stem: A Lightweight Safety Mechanism for Vision-Language-Action Models via Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Bojun Zou, Wenhao Yu, Jiaohao Li, Jiaxuan Lin, Guanting Ye, Haohan Geng, Weihao Yu, Yanyong Zhang, Jianmin Ji
papers.evidence: 施加强空间约束的强化学习安全机制
papers.tldr: VLA模型多面向无约束静态操作，忽视空间约束与动态障碍，而收集避障数据成本高且微调可能损伤原能力。VLA-Stem不改底层VLA策略，将动作块转为运动参考，并用强化学习训练Stem策略结合本体感知与局部障碍信息在推理时自适应修正执行。在六个受限仿真设置中，无碰撞任务成功率52.8%，显著高于最强安全基线23.7%，且无障碍时保持原策略性能。真实实验也显示静态与动态障碍下碰撞一致减少，为机器人执行提供轻量、类脑干的安全机制。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models integrate high-level reasoning with low-level action execution for end-to-end robotic control. However, most VLA models target static manipulation in unconstrained environments, overlooking spatial constraints and dynamic obstacles. Fine-tuning VLAs on obstacle-avoidance data is a straightforward solution, but collecting such data is costly, especially for dynamic scenarios, and may degrade their original task capabilities. To address these limitations, we propose VLA-Stem, a lightweight, reinforcement-learning-based safety mechanism for VLA systems. Without fine-tuning the underlying VLA policy, VLA-Stem converts its action chunks into motion references and uses trajectory-level guidance to preserve their spatial intent while allowing flexible motion and timing adjustments. Conditioned on these references, robot proprioception, and local obstacle information, the Stem policy adaptively modifies execution at inference time, preserving the original task intent while enabling responsive adaptation to spatial constraints and dynamic obstacles. For robust and sample-efficient training, we combine teacher-student distillation with curriculum learning. We evaluate VLA-Stem on reference following, static spatial constraints, and dynamic obstacle avoidance. Across six constrained simulation settings, VLA-Stem achieves 52.8% average collision-free task success versus 23.7% for the strongest safety baseline, while preserving base-policy performance in obstacle-free settings; real-world experiments further show consistent collision reductions under static and dynamic obstacles. These results demonstrate that VLA-Stem couples high-level VLA task intent with rapid, reflex-like responses to immediate physical risks, providing a brainstem-inspired mechanism for robust robot execution.
